body.p: A trickster. Dyaiku, a man, lives with his grandmother. They live in a tent. Their tent was very small. Dyaiku says to his grandmother: Grandma, I'll go and hunt. Well, go and hunt! Dyaiku left, bringing his bow. He took a bow made from a rib of a wild reindeer. And his arrow is from a willow. Dyaiku runs, walks during a whole day. Tents appear ahead. About ten tents appeared. Well, having seen the tents, he threw his bow and arrows on the earth. Among ten tents, he entered the middle one. In the middle tent (he came in; there are) seven giants Dyadyuru. He stopped by the the door. Dyaiku says: Seven Dyadyuru, which of you is runner, which is wrestler? A giant says: We cannot wrestle, we cannot run, Dyaiku. Dyaiku, be quiet. We are weak. The older brother of Dyadyuru says: We are weak. Sit down near our daughter. He sat down near Dyadyuru's daughter. He ate and prepared to sleep. Dyaiku fell asleep with Dyadyuru's daughter.why Lative? When they woke up, Dyaiku says: Well, is there something to hunt in this land? Then Dyadyuru says: There are wild reindeers. But we have no weapons to kill them. Dyaiku says: If there were weapons. As to my bow, I don't have it. I had it. But I broke it while coming here. It was my grandfather's bow. I got very angry, when I met two gangsters. So I met them, I got very angry and killed both. When I shot one of them, I broke my bow. The Dyadyuru says: Yes, we have a bow. Our forefather's bow is too heavy for our forces. Well, Dyaiku says: Let me see your forefather's bow. Dyadyuru says: Bring it in. They went and brought the bow, they brought it in. Dyaiku looked at it. A big thick (bow) made from a larch. They put it near Dyaiku. Dyaiku tried it: Ou, a huge (bow). Dyaiku tries to draw the bow string, (but) he cannot even bend it. Well, Dyaiku says: Maybe when my bones get warm, it'll be better, and I'll go to hunt. Well, Dyadyuru says: Our hunter will use the sledge. Dyaiku says: In my whole life a reindeer could not lift me. I don't need a reindeer. I'll go to hunt by foot. Well, Dyaiku went. He walks, dragging the bow. While he was walking, darkness fell. In the evening he found a little mountain range. Between two sides of the range there was a gully. It was, as if bitten [by this mountain range]. There were many wild reindeers. Seeing the reindeers, he stopped. He took off his coat. Taking his coat off, he waved it towards the reindeers. The startled reindeers ran away. Following the reindeers' traces, Dyaiku found a calf, trampled under reindeers' feet. Dyaiku cut it. Having cut it, he began to eat it raw. He began to eat the calf's meat raw, ate it all, together with the spinal cord, (picking it out) with his file-knife. He ate it all and divided the spine into bones. He divided all the ribs into bones. Along the reindeers' road he puts bones one by one â he dug in hundred stocks. One stock is a spine bone, one stock is a rib bone. While he did so, he made hundred stocks. So he did stocks, then he made a sign: he broke down all Dyadyuru's arrows and putzachem sjuda is'a? them above the stocks. He chipped Dyadyuru's bow, he broke it on his knee. Having broken it, on the same place he threw it away. He came back to the tents. He came back in the night. In the tents, they fell asleep long ago. Dyaiku went to sleep to Dyadyuru's daughter. All his boots are stained with blood. Arms are bloody up to the elbows. Dyaiku is sleeping. His fellows woke up. Dyadyuru's wife says to her daughter: Your fellow came tonight. Why didn't you even get up? He went to sleep without eating. Speak quietly, our hunter is tired. Don't wake him. Well, Dyaiku woke up and says: I am so tired. Dyadyuru says: What has our hunter killed? How many (reindeers) has he killed? Well, I have killed reindeers, you can't even count them. I have made stocks, maybe hundred stocks. (I've put) ten reindeers in each stock, in some stocks more than ten. Having killed the reindeers, I got into trouble. What, how did you do? I broke the bow, which I was carrying, when I was killing the last reindeer. My bones had warmed up, and so the bow was broken. Oh, it doesn't matter. If you had killed (something) for us to eat, let it be broken. Well, when you go for the reindeers, I think, you should bring all the sledges from all the tents. Will it be enough sledges? Let all the people go that are there. And let the others harness four reindeers in each sledge. I am very tired. I will sleep all that time. They went away for the wild reindeers, everbody had gone. As soon as they had gone, he, Dyaiku, went away in the tundra. Dyaiku walks. He came to his grandmother's tent, then says: Grandma, I've got into trouble. Dyadyuru will come soon. They will probably kill me. Bring in your grave- clothes. Grandma, I'll be your daughter. I'll put on (your) clothes. Dyaiku put on his grandmother's clothes. Grandma, treat me as your daughter. On Dyaiku's traces came a sledge. Seven Dyadyuru came. They (use) their bows instead of whips. They stopped near Dyaiku's tent. The seven Dyadyuru came into the tent. They are looking all around the tent. Where is Dyaiku? Where are you looking for Dyaiku? A lot of people had taken him away, before you came. Why (are you looking for) Dyaiku? Is he still alive? He would be killed anyway. The other Dyadyurus say: It turns out that Dyaiku has a sister. Let us bring away the girl! Hey, my brother is not here. How will you take me away? Dyadyuru says: It doesn't matter, we'll bring you away. They roused Dyaiku, put him into the sledge, then Dyadyurus came back. Dyadyurus came to their tents. They brought Dyaiku, the girl, into a tent. They gave him to the son of Dyadyuru (as a wife). Dyaiku does not even want to eat. Dyaiku is always outdoors, doesn't want to (come in). When they fell asleep, Dyaiku escaped to the tundra. He reached his grandmother's tent and put on his own clothes. NEE059694
